summary: An episode on elite panic, the tendency of people in power to fear ordinary people in disasters, told through the 2004 Ycua Bolanos supermarket fire in Paraguay, where exits were locked, and the armed crackdowns after the San Francisco and Anchorage earthquakes.

evidence.note: Supermarket fire in August 2004 after years of gas building up in the roof
Retrial after riots raises sentences for owner, son and guard; retrial year from outside knowledge
Host names elite panic, a phenomenon rather than a person, as the episode's real subject
1906 San Francisco earthquake and mutual aid segment begins
General Funston imposes martial law; mayor authorises shooting of supposed looters
Katrina: officials and media spread false violence rumours that delayed rescues
Anchorage earthquake segment; police deputise drunk volunteers and halt survivor search

notes: Primary subject is a concept, not a person; no theme exists for disaster response, so moral-panics (elites fearing an exaggerated mob threat) is the closest fit. Host dates the Alaska quake to 1962; it was 1964. The Paraguay retrial verdict (2008) is not dated in the transcript. Paiva's birth year is not clearly stated, so floruit is used. COVID and de Blasio get only a brief mention.
